Scale-free nonprofit density

Source: R/scale-free-density.R
get_scale_free_density.Rd

Measures whether a market has more or fewer nonprofits (and more or less of a resource) than expected for its population. Within each subsector and year, the number of nonprofits and the resource total are modeled as a power function of population across markets, and each market's observed value is compared with the value expected for its size.

Usage

get_scale_free_density(
  df,
  geography = "CENSUS_CBSA_FIPS",
  population = "POP_METRO",
  subsector = "NTEEV2",
  year = "TAXYEAR",
  resource = "TOTREV",
  pop_table = NULL,
  model = c("negbin", "poisson", "loglinear")
)

Arguments

df

A data frame with one row per organization-year.

geography

Name of the column that identifies the market's geography, such as "CENSUS_CBSA_FIPS" or "COUNTY_FIPS".

population

Name of the column that holds the market's population, such as "POP_METRO" or "POP_COUNTY". Ignored, and may be NULL, when pop_table is supplied.

subsector

Name of the column that identifies the subsector. When it is "NTEEV2", the first three characters (the major group) are used.

year

Name of the column that identifies the year, such as "TAXYEAR".

resource

Name of the numeric column that measures organization size, such as "TOTREV", "TOTEXP" or "NETASS". Negative values are set to zero.

pop_table

Optional data frame of market populations with columns GEO, YEAR and POP. Supply it so that markets with no organizations at all are still included. When NULL, market populations are taken from the population column of df, so only markets with at least one organization (in any subsector) are included.

model

How the expected values are estimated:

  • "negbin" (default): negative binomial regression of the count on log population, which handles zero counts and overdispersion. Falls back to Poisson when the negative binomial fit fails.

  • "poisson": Poisson regression of the count on log population.

  • "loglinear": least squares regression of log(N + 1) on log(POP + 1), the original method.

For the resource total, both count options use Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood (a quasi-Poisson GLM), which is suited to non-negative dollar amounts with many zeros.

Value

A tibble with one row per GEO, SUB and YEAR, containing N, POP, the summed resource, LOG_NPO, LOG_POP, LOG_<resource>, EXPECTED_N, EXPECTED_<resource>, DENSITY_PCTL_N, DENSITY_PCTL_R (both capped at 2) and the fitted models in the list columns model_n and model_r. The model type is stored in the "density_model" attribute.

Rows with SUB = "ALL" cover all subsectors in a market. Rows with GEO = "ALL" are national totals: their POP is the summed population of the markets, and their density values are NA because they are not part of the cross-market models.

Details

The density index is observed / expected - 1: 0 means the market matches the expected density for its size, 0.5 means 50% more than expected, and -1 means none at all. The "loglinear" model computes it as exp(residual) - 1 on the log(x + 1) scale, which compresses differences among small markets.

Every market in the population frame appears in every subsector, with N = 0 where it has no organizations, so the models are not limited to markets that happen to have an organization in that subsector. Organizations are counted whether or not their resource value is missing; the resource total ignores missing values.

Examples

d <- get_scale_free_density( npo_panel_sample,
                             geography = "COUNTY_FIPS",
                             population = "POP_COUNTY" )
head( d[ d$SUB == "ALL", c( "GEO", "YEAR", "N", "EXPECTED_N", "DENSITY_PCTL_N" ) ] )
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   GEO    YEAR     N EXPECTED_N DENSITY_PCTL_N
#>   <chr> <int> <int>      <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 50001  2015   124       102.          0.216
#> 2 50001  2016   122       103.          0.184
#> 3 50001  2017   122       105.          0.165
#> 4 50001  2018   123       106.          0.161
#> 5 50001  2019   126       106.          0.189
#> 6 50003  2015   121       102.          0.181
